summary.headline: ISGEC Q1 FY27 standalone total income up 51% to INR 1,585 crore, but PBT up only 10% to INR 123 crore; FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%.
summary.overview: Standalone total income rose 51% YoY to INR 1,585 crore and EBIT grew 15% to INR 157 crore, with PBT up 10% to INR 123 crore as Q1 FY26 had high forex-driven other income. Manufacturing EBIT margin was 12% and projects EBIT margin 5.25%. Consolidated PBT was INR 53 crore, held back by an INR 83 crore loss at the Philippines ethanol plant, which ran at about 65-70% utilisation. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 10-12% and said it is conservative, citing carry-forward of order execution into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: about 45% higher vs INR 1,374 crore in Q1 FY26
includes INR 37 crore depreciation, INR 20 crore interest, INR 10 crore forex
vs INR 381 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and INR 408 crore at 30 Jun 2025
down INR 170 crore QoQ from INR 476 crore; INR 832 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Industrial Projects (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income up on improved execution per schedule; management expects roughly INR 1,000 crore per quarter in Q2 FY27 and projects EBIT margin of 5-6% for FY27. Export orders booked in Africa and Latin America.

segments.name: Manufacturing (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income lifted by dispatch of a roughly INR 130 crore US order that had been on hold; EBIT margin 12%, guided 12-13%. Steady-state consolidated manufacturing revenue guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen
segments.commentary: Orders in hand INR 889 crore. FY26 revenue about INR 670 crore; management expects about 10% growth in revenue and profit in FY27.

segments.name: Saraswati Sugar Mills
segments.commentary: Revenue down due to lower cane availability last season (untimely rain); cane availability improvement steps under way for next season.

segments.name: Philippines ethanol (CBPI)
segments.commentary: Q1 loss INR 83 crore at about 65-70% utilisation; crushed about 84,000 tonnes of cane, sold over 8 million litres of ethanol. Management targets about 90% utilisation by December and a much lower loss in Q2.

segments.name: Eagle Press and Isgec Titan Metal
segments.commentary: Eagle Press about INR 150 crore a year; Isgec Titan Metal expected at about INR 150 crore in FY27 vs INR 102 crore in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at 10-12%; management says the figure is conservative with a bias to realism.
Manufacturing EBIT margin guided at 12-13% for FY27; projects EBIT margin guided to improve slightly within 5-6%.
Isgec Hitachi Zosen revenue and profit guided about 10% higher than FY26.
Manufacturing capacity expansion (approved INR 502 crore) to add up to about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue when fully complete; main benefit from FY28-29.

Bhartauli machine-building phase 1 (INR 73 crore) to complete in early September 2026, with about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential; billing expected only from Q1 FY28 as work-in-progress builds first.
Dahej skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Philippines ethanol depreciation expected about INR 95 crore in FY27 (WDV method); interest about INR 19-20 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Bhartauli (Haryana) presses plant: phase 1 INR 70-73 crore completing first week of September 2026; phase 2 (INR 218 crore) completion expected around end-CY2027 or Q1 CY2028.
Dahej (Gujarat) SEZ skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Casting factory expansions, tubing and piping shops at Rattangarh and standard mechanical press factory at Bawal are running largely on schedule, with some facilities completing in FY27.
Board-approved manufacturing capex INR 502 crore; separate corporate office building under construction in projects business.
Q1 capex about INR 47 crore, funded from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong across almost all product lines; export inquiry base described as healthy.
Export orders booked in Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia; more than INR 750 crore of export orders booked in Q1.
Standalone orders of about INR 1,200 crore booked in July to date (Q2 FY27).
Management says INR 95/USD rupee improves competitiveness versus other bidders; export logistics costs, freight rates and transit times have risen due to the geopolitical situation.

Commodity prices (steel, copper, aluminium, nickel) stabilised but slightly above pre-war levels; war-related material cost increases have a small adverse effect on profitability, absorbed through contingencies.
Project mix shifting to shorter-duration (max 33-36 months, target 2-2.5 years) technology-intensive orders; avoiding long contract/site-erection-heavy orders.
Sugar machinery export orders up, particularly sugar refineries; management declined to detail the large export orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 top-line guidance only 10-12% despite strong execution and a larger order book, and what is the quarterly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a good part of order execution carries forward into FY28, which is why guidance is 10-12%. Projects are expected at about INR 1,000 crore a quarter and standalone manufacturing at a similar level in Q2 FY27, with Isgec Hitachi Zosen about 10% higher than FY26's roughly INR 670 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state manufacturing revenue on a consolidated basis, and how big was the Q1 US order?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated manufacturing was about INR 800 crore in Q1 and is guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter for the next quarter, rising a bit later. The delayed US order was about INR 130 crore; the customer had paid 95% two or three quarters earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance conservative when Q1 alone adds about INR 570 crore of incremental revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers a conservative guidance it can meet over an aggressive one. It agreed the numbers could be higher and said there is hope for better outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and revenue potential of the expansions, and when will they be complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Board-approved manufacturing capex is INR 502 crore; the corporate office in projects is separate. Full completion could add about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue, mostly from FY28-29. Bhartauli phase 1 (INR 73 crore) completes in early September 2026 with about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential, but billing starts only in Q1 FY28 as work-in-progress builds; phase 2 (INR 218 crore) completes around end-CY2027 or Q1 CY2028. Dahej completes around 31 May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Philippines ethanol plant post an INR 83 crore loss, and when does it reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: The loss comprised about INR 37 crore depreciation, INR 20 crore interest, INR 10 crore forex and unrecovered fixed costs. Utilisation is 65-70%; management targets about 90% in December and a substantially lower loss in Q2, with the plant running on molasses until the next cane season starts in November.

qa_highlights.question: How much depreciation and interest does the Philippines business carry, and is shutting or selling it an option?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 depreciation is expected at about INR 95 crore on a WDV basis, so roughly INR 57-60 crore over the remaining three quarters. Interest is about INR 19-20 crore per quarter, paid to the parent. Management said it considers all options, but a shut asset would find no buyer, and it is hopeful the plant will begin to cover interest and costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone PBT grow only 10% when EBITDA grew about 64%, and what drove other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY26 other income was high due to dividends from subsidiaries (about INR 20-22 crore a year, now split across quarters), interest income and forex gains on Philippines loans. Forex will keep swinging other income up and down; management said operating income was the better measure this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the export order intake, and what are the execution timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: More than INR 750 crore of export orders were booked in Q1, from Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia, with sugar refinery machinery up. Management cited INR 95/USD as a competitive help, offset by higher freight and transit times. Execution timelines are about 4-12 months for manufactured items, 14 months to 2.5 years for projects, 15-18 months at Isgec Hitachi Zosen and 6-9 months at Eagle Press.

risks_watch: Philippines ethanol plant: utilisation has been 65-70% and it must reach about 90% by December to cover roughly INR 40 crore a quarter of depreciation and interest for PBT breakeven; the Q2 loss reduction is the key check.
Execution timing of INR 130 crore order-on-hold type dispatches and Bhartauli phase 1 billing, which starts only in Q1 FY28, so revenue visibility from new capacity in FY27 is limited.

Export logistics and war-related costs: freight rates, container availability and transit times have worsened; commodity prices remain slightly above pre-war levels and absorption relies on contingencies.
Decline in other income (forex and dividend timing) can keep PBT growth well below EBITDA growth; there is no firm guidance on capitalisation or depreciation step-up for FY27.
Saraswati Sugar Mills revenue is expected to fall on low cane availability; cane availability steps are under way for the next season.
Management declined to quantify several items (large export orders, FY27 Philippines EBITDA at 90% utilisation, capitalisation), so these should be tracked in next quarter's disclosures.
key_quotes: So the order book, I agree, has improved substantially. But a good part of the order executions is going to carry forward to the next financial year.
It's better to give a conservative guidance and meet it rather than give an aggressive guidance and be uncertain about it.
We are being realistic with a conservative bias.
Now what we are taking maximum is something like 2.5 years at the most 33-36 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic demand, execution and margins, but deliberately conservative on FY27 top-line guidance and cautious on the Philippines ethanol business. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on the ethanol EBITDA outlook, export order sizes and capitalisation.
